items.label: Unit frames
items.desc: Our player, target, target-of-target, focus and pet frames, in place of Blizzard's.

items.label: Party frames
items.desc: Our party frames. Turn off to use the game's (for example its raid-style party frames).

items.label: Boss frames
items.desc: Frames for up to five bosses, down the right side of the screen. They appear during boss fights; click one to target it.

items.label: Arena enemy frames
items.desc: Frames for up to five arena enemies, down the right side of the screen, in place of the game's own. Left-click one to target it, right-click to set it as your focus. With enemy cooldowns on, their trinket, interrupt and dispel sit beside them.

items.label: Focus's target frame
items.desc: A small frame for whatever your focus is targeting, like the target's target frame. It appears only while your focus has a target.

items.label: Raid frames
items.desc: Raid frames in our style.

items.label: Resource % on frames & nameplates
items.desc: Shows mana, rage, energy or whatever the resource is as a percentage: on every unit frame that has a power bar, and beside the bar on nameplates of units that have a resource.

items.label: Health as numbers, not %
items.desc: Health on the unit frames, raid frames and nameplates is shown as an amount (12.4k) instead of a percentage.

items.label: Mana & resources as numbers, not %
items.desc: Mana, rage, energy and the rest are shown as an amount instead of a percentage.

items.label: XP & reputation as numbers, not %
items.desc: The experience and reputation bar shows amounts (2,340 / 8,800) instead of a percentage.

items.label: Player cast bar
items.desc: Our cast bar for your own spells.

items.label: Crafting bar & profession icons
items.desc: While you craft, the progress bar in the profession window is replaced by one in our style, and its icon is the profession's own (leatherworking, alchemy, cooking and the rest) instead of the game's placeholder. The ordinary cast bar shows the same icon while you craft.

items.label: Swing timers
items.desc: Bars that fill as your next melee or ranged swing comes up, with an out-of-range note.

items.label: Consumables bar
items.desc: A small bar that fills itself with the potions, bandages, food and drink, flasks, elixirs and scrolls in your bags, one button each, with how many you have. Click to use. It is laid out again between fights; place it in move mode.

items.label: Buff & debuff bars
items.desc: Your buffs and debuffs in our style.

items.label: XP / reputation bar
items.desc: A slim experience and reputation bar; hover it for pace and time to level.

items.label: Breath & fatigue bar
items.desc: Our own bar for breath underwater, fatigue when you swim too far out, and feign death, in place of the game's.

items.label: Combat timer
items.desc: A small timer that counts how long the fight has lasted, whatever your role. It shows the final time for a few seconds afterwards, then goes. It can be moved like any panel.

items.label: Nameplates
items.desc: Restyled bars over enemies' heads, colored by threat.

items.label: Nameplates: quest marks
items.desc: A yellow ! beside the nameplate of anything you still need for a quest, so it can be picked out of a pack at a glance.

items.label: Nameplate casts & debuffs
items.desc: A cast bar under each enemy nameplate.

items.label: Nameplate health text
items.desc: Shows health on each nameplate's bar: a percentage, or the amount if "Health as numbers, not %" is switched on, beside it.

items.label: Action bars
items.desc: Restyled action bars, and a Menu button in place of the game's micro menu.

items.label: Fantasy Glass action bars
items.desc: Our own action bars in place of the game's: eight bars of real action buttons, each with its own number of buttons, rows, size, spacing and direction, set at once below without the game's Edit Mode. Bar 1 changes page with your stance, form or stealth. Your key bindings press them. Needs Action bars on, and a /reload.

items.label: Cooldown numbers
items.desc: Seconds remaining, as numbers, on action buttons.

items.label: Action bars: key text
items.desc: The key each action button is bound to, in its top right corner. Switch off for buttons with no key text. Takes effect at once.

items.label: Action bars: macro names
items.desc: The name of a macro, along the bottom of its button. Takes effect at once.

items.label: Role HUD
items.desc: A small display in the middle of the screen for your role: threat, party health, or target health.

items.label: Class resources (under your frame)
items.desc: Under your frame: your class's second resource (holy power, soul shards, chi and so on), rune cooldowns, your mana while in a form, and a hunter's pet happiness. Only what your class and this game have is shown.

items.label: Class resource you design (Bars and frames)
items.desc: Your combo points, holy power, soul shards, chi, arcane charges, essence or runes, shown the way you design it below (Class resource): dots, a bar or a number, any size, anywhere.

items.label: Totem timers
items.desc: An icon for each active totem with its time left.

items.label: Weapon imbue reminder
items.desc: A note when your weapon imbue (or poison) is missing or about to run out.

items.label: Aggro warning (in groups)
items.desc: A warning when a monster turns on you in a group and you are not the tank.

items.label: Cooldown tracker
items.desc: A row of abilities you choose, each showing its cooldown. Choose them below.

items.label: Custom alerts
items.desc: Alerts you make yourself, below: when your health or mana is low, a buff is missing, an ability is ready, your target casts, your bags are nearly full... show a line, play a sound, or say it.

items.label: Spoken alerts
items.desc: Says things aloud with the game's own text-to-speech voice: ready checks, whispers, missing buffs, loss of control and your custom alerts. Choose which below.

items.label: Cooldown timeline
items.desc: The abilities on your cooldown tracker list sliding along one slim bar towards ready, with the last seconds stretched out so they are easy to read. In a fight the game may hide cooldowns: those wait at the right end with the game's own sweep.

items.label: Cooldown pulse
items.desc: When an ability on the cooldown tracker comes off cooldown, its icon appears in the middle of the screen for a moment. Choose the abilities below; place the pulse in move mode.

items.label: Buff alerts
items.desc: A large icon when a buff you chose is on you. Choose them below.

items.label: Loot browser: what bosses drop
items.desc: Notes what each boss drops as you kill it in raids and dungeons - from your loot window, the loot rolls and what anyone in your group loots - shared by all your characters. /fgui drops shows it, raid by raid and boss by boss, with the upgrades for you first. On clients with the dungeon journal, its loot lists are there too. Click an item to star it for your wishlist (/fgui wish): you are told when it drops or comes up in a roll.

items.label: Boss tooltips: what it drops for me
items.desc: Point at a boss and its tooltip lists what it drops that is on your wishlist or would be an upgrade for you, with how often you have seen it drop. From the loot browser's book (and the dungeon journal where the game has one).

items.label: Threat meter (in groups)
items.desc: A small panel of its own: in a group, with a hostile target, who has how much threat on it, most first, up to five of you. Your row turns the warning color near the top and the danger color when you would pull the target. Works without the damage meter. Move it with /fgui move.

items.label: Farming sessions (/fgui farm)
items.desc: /fgui farm starts a session: a small panel shows the time and what you make an hour, in gold and in the items you loot (the auction price you have seen, or the vendor's). /fgui farm again lists every item; /fgui farm stop ends it, and the session counts in your weekly recap.

items.label: Run log: dungeon and raid times (/fgui runs)
items.desc: Each dungeon and raid you go into is a run: how long it took, the bosses killed and when, the wipes on each, your deaths and your rare and better loot. /fgui runs lists them place by place, each with its best time (the quickest of the runs that killed the most bosses). Stepping out to repair is still the same run.

items.label: Whose upgrade: boss drops in a group
items.desc: When a boss drops something rare or better, the players in your group who use Fantasy Glass UI each work out whether it is an upgrade for them and quietly tell the others. A small panel says whose upgrade it is and by how many item levels, before anyone rolls. Nothing is said in chat. Move it with /fgui move.

items.label: Group gear check (/fgui gear)
items.desc: /fgui gear lists everyone in your party or raid with their item level, the lowest first, and the group's average. The game sends another player's gear one player at a time and only within reach, so the list fills in while it is open; it never asks during a fight or while your own inspect window is open.

items.label: Lifetime stats (/fgui stats)
items.desc: /fgui stats: one page of totals for this character and for all of them together - time played, levels, quests, kills, deaths, gold made and spent, items looted, bosses killed, dungeon and raid runs with their best times, and time spent farming. The counts start the day this version first runs.

items.label: Damage meter (if available)
items.desc: A damage and healing meter, on clients that share those totals. Views: damage and healing per second, damage and healing done, damage taken, absorbs, interrupts, dispels and deaths. Click its heading (or roll the mouse wheel over it) for the next view, right-click for this fight, overall or an earlier fight, Shift-right-click to reset. Point at a row for that player's abilities. Your own row has a white edge. Under the bars: who has how much threat on your target when you are in a group.

items.label: Damage meter: drawer on the chat box
items.desc: The damage meter comes out of the side of the chat box, as tall as the chat box. The small tab on its edge tucks it away and brings it out again (so does /fgui meter). Switch this off to have the meter as a window of its own that you place in move mode.

items.label: Damage meter: open in combat
items.desc: The meter's drawer comes out by itself when a fight starts and tucks itself away eight seconds after it ends. Open or close it yourself and it is left as you set it. Needs the drawer on the chat box.

items.label: Combat start and end alerts
items.desc: A word in the middle of the screen as a fight starts (+ Combat) and as it ends (- Combat), gone in a moment. Place it in move mode.

items.label: Raid tools panel
items.desc: A small panel for ready checks, pull timers and markers when you lead a group.

items.label: Hide the game's raid manager
items.desc: Hides the game's raid manager, the panel that slides out from the left edge of the screen in a group. The Raid tools panel has ready checks, markers and role polls, and leaving a group is in the game menu or on your portrait. If you use the game's own raid frames, its group filters (which groups to show) go with it.

items.label: Group cooldowns panel
items.desc: A small panel, in a group, listing who has a battle resurrection, an interrupt, a big defensive or a raid cooldown, and whether it is ready or how long until it is. Group members with Fantasy Glass UI tell each other (whether or not this panel is on); others are not listed.

items.label: Interrupt rotation
items.desc: A small bar in a group saying who is next to interrupt, and telling you (on screen, and aloud if spoken alerts are on) when it is you. Set the order with /fgui kicks <name> <name>; the group leader's order is shared. Needs the group cooldowns from players with Fantasy Glass UI. /fgui testgroup shows it with made-up group mates.

items.label: Boss notes
items.desc: A note for each boss: a tactic, who soaks, when to use a cooldown. It opens when you target the boss, when the fight starts, or with a pull timer. /fgui bossnote writes one; the group's leader can send theirs to the group.

items.label: Death recap
items.desc: When you die, the last hits and heals you took, with how long before the end. /fgui death shows it again.

items.label: Raid frames: mark missing buffs I can give
items.desc: A small icon on the raid and party frames of anyone missing the buff you can give (Fortitude, Mark of the Wild, Arcane Intellect, Battle Shout). Checked out of fights. /fgui testgroup shows it on sample frames.

items.label: Enemy trinket, interrupt and dispel cooldowns
items.desc: In arenas and battlegrounds: an enemy player's PvP trinket, interrupt and dispel, counting down once they have used it. Beside the arena enemy frames, and under your target and focus frames. Only spells the game names to add-ons can be seen.

items.label: Mount and pet buttons
items.desc: Two small buttons you can move anywhere: a random favorite mount (one that suits where you are; click again to get off) and a random favorite pet. Both have key bindings too (Key Bindings, AddOns).

items.label: Tooltips: who of your characters can make it
items.desc: Item tooltips say which of your characters can make the item, from the recipes noted when each opens a profession window. /fgui crafts searches them all.

items.label: Totem bar (Shamans)
items.desc: Four buttons, one for each element. Left-click drops the totem chosen for it, right-click takes the one that is down away, and the mouse wheel over a button chooses another (not in a fight). The totem that is down shows with its time left. Only for Shamans.

items.label: Accept setups other players send me
items.desc: When another player sends you a layout, profile or theme (/fgui send), it opens in the preview, where you choose whether to take it. Off: anything sent is ignored.

items.label: Missing buff reminder
items.desc: Buffs that should always be on you (Lightning Shield, a seal, an aura): an icon with a ! shows while one is missing. Choose them with /fgui remind and the buff's name. Not shown while dead, on a flight, or resting in a city.

items.label: Buff filter & my debuffs rimmed
items.desc: Leaves buffs you choose out of your own buff row (/fgui hidebuff and the buff's name), and gives your own debuffs on other units a rim in the accent color.

items.label: Focus cast alert
items.desc: A sound and a line in the middle of the screen when an enemy you have as your focus starts a cast.

items.label: Execute line on the target
items.desc: A thin line on the target's health bar at a percentage you choose, 20 unless you change it with /fgui execute.

items.label: Loss-of-control alert
items.desc: A large icon with a countdown while you are stunned, silenced, feared or otherwise not in control. Place it in move mode.

items.label: Boss and dungeon timer
items.desc: A small panel with the time on the current boss and the time since you entered the dungeon or raid. When a boss dies you are told the time and your best, from the run log (/fgui runs), so the two always agree.

items.label: Keys for my best potion and food
items.desc: Two key bindings (the game's Key Bindings, under AddOns): one always uses a healthstone or your best healing potion, the other eats and drinks your best food. Kept up to date as your bags change, between fights.

items.label: Travel bar
items.desc: Your hearthstone and every teleport or portal you know, on one bar with their cooldowns. Place it in move mode.

items.label: Home key (best way home)
items.desc: A key binding (Key Bindings, AddOns) for the best way home that is ready: your hearthstone, then Astral Recall, then a teleport. /fgui home says which it would use.

items.label: Open-all button
items.desc: A button that appears while something in your bags can be opened (a clam, a bag of loot, an unlocked lockbox). Each click opens one.

items.label: Minimap
items.desc: A square minimap with zone, coordinates and clock.

items.label: Minimap: round
items.desc: A round minimap instead of the square one, with a rim in your theme's color. The zone, coordinates and clock stay on it.

items.label: Minimap: diamond
items.desc: A diamond minimap, cut like the Starcut portrait, with a fine rim and a star on each point. It takes the place of round or square while it is on. The zone, coordinates and clock stay on it.

items.label: Pixel-perfect scale
items.desc: Sets the whole interface to the scale where one of its pixels is one of your screen's, so thin rims and lettering stay sharp. Switching it off puts back the scale the game had. Interface size, in Look and themes › Accessibility, still works on top of it.

items.label: Minimap button collector
items.desc: Gathers other add-ons' minimap buttons into one fold-out panel.

items.label: Minimap button for these options
items.desc: A small button on the minimap with the add-on's icon. Left-click opens these options, right-click starts moving panels, and it can be dragged along the minimap.

items.label: Coordinates on the world map
items.desc: Shows where you are, and where the mouse is pointing, in the bottom left corner of the world map.

items.label: Rare spawn alert
items.desc: Tells you once, with a sound, when the game marks a rare creature, treasure or event on your minimap.

items.label: Rare spawn memory on the map
items.desc: Remembers where the rare alert spotted each rare or treasure, and marks them on the world map. Only what you have found yourself. /fgui rares lists them.

items.label: Minimap: right-click for tracking
items.desc: Right-click the minimap to open the game's tracking menu.

items.label: Minimap: who pinged
items.desc: When someone pings the minimap, their name is shown on it for a moment.

items.label: World map: group in class colors
items.desc: Your party or raid on the world map as dots in class colors; point at one for the name. The game gives no positions inside dungeons and raids.

items.label: Smaller world map
items.desc: The world map opens at three quarters of its size (/fgui mapsize to change) and fades while you move, so you can walk with it open.

items.label: Flight timer
items.desc: A bar with the time left on a flight path. A route's time is learned the first time you fly it; until then the bar counts up.

items.label: Info bar
items.desc: A thin bar at the top: frame rate, latency, durability, gold and time.

items.label: Info bar: bags, friends, guild
items.desc: Adds free bag slots, friends and guild online, and a mail note to the info bar.

items.label: Info bar: other add-ons' data
items.desc: Shows the data other add-ons publish (through LibDataBroker) in a strip under the info bar.

items.label: Clock: 12-hour
items.desc: Clocks read 3:05pm instead of 15:05. Takes effect at once. Presets never change this.

items.label: Clock: server time
items.desc: Clocks show the game server's time instead of your computer's. Takes effect at once. Presets never change this.

items.label: Windows & menus
items.desc: Restyles the game's own windows, menus and dialogs to match.

items.label: Spellbook
items.desc: Restyles the spellbook.

items.label: Character window
items.desc: Restyles the character window and all its pages.

items.label: Character window: gear set buttons
items.desc: A row of buttons under the character window, one for each set saved in the game's equipment manager. Click one to put that set on. The set you are wearing is underlined; a set with pieces you no longer have is gray. Not in combat.

items.label: Gear set name over my player frame
items.desc: The name of the gear set you are wearing, small, over the top right of your player frame. Put a set on with /fgui set <name>, or give the first five sets keys (Key Bindings, Fantasy Glass UI).

items.label: Character window: talent set buttons
items.desc: A small 1 and 2 at the top of the character window: one click changes talent set (also /fgui spec).

items.label: Character window: missing enchants
items.desc: On the character window, a red E on a piece with no enchant where one usually goes, and a G where a gem socket is empty.

items.label: Item levels when inspecting
items.desc: On the inspect window, shows the item level of each piece the other player wears and their average, like your own character window.

items.label: Drag the game's windows
items.desc: Drag the character window, spellbook, vendor, mailbox and the game's other windows by any empty part of them; each opens where you left it. "Reset window positions" in Layout and profiles puts them all back. Protected windows cannot be moved during combat.

items.label: Tooltips
items.desc: Restyled tooltips with class colors.

items.label: Item counts in tooltips
items.desc: Adds how many of an item you own, across characters, to its tooltip.

items.label: Item level & price in tooltips
items.desc: Adds item level and vendor price to item tooltips when the game doesn't show them.

items.label: Item & spell IDs in tooltips
items.desc: Adds the item's or spell's ID number to its tooltip, for writing macros. Presets never change this.

items.label: Player tooltips: choose the lines
items.desc: Lets you choose every line of a player's tooltip with the switches below it. Off, the game's lines stay as they are.

items.label: Player tooltips: title in the name
items.desc: Their title in front of their name ("Champion of the Frozen Wastes" and the like).

items.label: Player tooltips: realm in the name
items.desc: The realm after the name of a player from another realm.

items.label: Player tooltips: guild
items.desc: The line with their guild's name.

items.label: Player tooltips: guild rank
items.desc: Their rank in their guild, under the guild's name.

items.label: Player tooltips: level, race and class
items.desc: The line with their level, race and class.

items.label: Player tooltips: faction
items.desc: The line saying Alliance or Horde.

items.label: Player tooltips: PvP
items.desc: The line saying they are flagged for PvP.

items.label: Player tooltips: health bar
items.desc: The health bar under a player's tooltip.

items.label: Player tooltips: who they target
items.desc: Who they have targeted ("Targeting: YOU" when it is you).

items.label: Player tooltips: role in your group
items.desc: Tank, healer or damage, as chosen in your group. Only while you are in a group.

items.label: Player tooltips: friend or guild mate
items.desc: "Your friend" or "In your guild" under players you know.

items.label: Player tooltips: health in numbers
items.desc: Their health in numbers: 12,345 / 20,000 (62%).

items.label: Player tooltips: hide during fights
items.desc: Puts player tooltips away while you are fighting, so they don't cover the fight. Hold Shift to see one anyway.

items.label: Quest tracker
items.desc: Our list of tracked quests at the side of the screen.

items.label: Goals panel
items.desc: A small panel of what you are working towards, with a bar each: reputations (/fgui goal rep <name>), gold on all your characters (/fgui goal gold 10000), a level (/fgui goal level 60), a mount (/fgui goal mount <name>), achievements, your own goals, and items (/fgui goal and a shift-clicked item with a number), counted on all your characters, with where a boss drop drops in its tooltip. A goal reached says so once.

items.label: Quest tracker: rewards
items.desc: The experience and money each quest gives, beside its name on the tracker; in gold once the quest is ready to turn in.

items.label: Quest log (L / /ql)
items.desc: Our quest log window (L, or /ql).

items.label: Quest banners & reward hint
items.desc: A banner when a quest is accepted or completed, and a hint at the best-selling reward.

items.label: Quest sounds
items.desc: A chime when one of a quest's objectives is finished, and the quest-complete sound when the whole quest is ready to hand in.

items.label: Auto accept/turn in quests
items.desc: Accepts and turns in quests for you without asking.

items.label: Glossy bar texture
items.desc: A glossy texture on health and power bars instead of a flat one.

items.label: Theme by place
items.desc: Switches to the theme you chose for cities and inns, dungeons, raids or everywhere else, as you travel. Choose them below. Only between themes of the same family.

items.label: Login splash
items.desc: As you log in, the add-on's emblem, your character and where you are, for a moment. Click to close it sooner. (The loading screen itself is the game's: add-ons cannot draw over it.)

items.label: "Loaded" line in chat at login
items.desc: The one line in chat when you log in, with the version. Off: Fantasy Glass UI only speaks up in chat when something needs you (a new version, a problem).

items.label: Login briefing: what is waiting
items.desc: A few seconds after you log in, one small window says what is waiting: crafts ready, mail on your other characters, lockouts that have reset, rested experience and the jobs left on your checklist. Only when something is waiting; /fgui briefing shows it at any time.

items.label: Weekly recap
items.desc: Notes each character's week as you play it: gold made or spent, time played, levels, raids and dungeons, best loot. /fgui recap shows the last week; the login briefing says when a new one is ready.

items.label: Milestones: a notice when one is reached
items.desc: A short notice and a sound when you reach a milestone: 100, 1,000, 10,000 kills; 100 quests; your first boss and your 100th; your first run; 1,000 gold made; and more. They are listed with the day on the stats page (/fgui stats). Needs Lifetime stats.

items.label: Boss guide: abilities from the journal
items.desc: When you target or pull a boss, its abilities from the game's dungeon journal show one line each under your boss note, with their icons. Only on game clients with the journal, and never while you have the journal open yourself. Needs Boss notes.

items.label: Combat text in your lettering
items.desc: The numbers that float up in combat use the add-on's lettering. The game reads that font as the world loads, so a change shows after a relog.

items.label: Rounded corners (glass)
items.desc: Rounded corners on panels and buttons, on glass themes.

items.label: Ring round the mouse pointer
items.desc: A ring in the accent color round the mouse pointer, so it is easy to find in a fight. It hides while you hold a mouse button to turn or look around.

items.label: Quieter red error line
items.desc: Drops the red lines that repeat constantly in a fight: not enough mana or rage, not ready yet, out of range, wrong facing, no target. Everything else the game says there still shows. Presets never change this.

items.label: Panels snap to each other
items.desc: In move mode, a panel you drag snaps to the edges of nearby panels as well as to the grid, so things line up. Hold Shift to place freely.

items.label: Notifications (loot, mail, warnings)
items.desc: Small notifications for an item you looted (uncommon or better), a new level, new mail, whispers, bags that are almost full and gear that needs repair.

items.label: Captions for sounds
items.desc: A line on screen for whatever gets your attention with a sound: a ready check, a whisper, a queue that is ready, a group invite, a duel, a boss emote, a raid warning, a roll on loot, the aggro warning and your own alerts. Each has a mark for its kind. For playing with the sound off, or for anyone who cannot hear it.

items.label: Ready check alert
items.desc: When someone starts a ready check: a sound that plays even with the game in another window, the game's icon flashing in the taskbar, and a notice saying who asked.

items.label: Queue alert
items.desc: When a dungeon finder or battleground invitation arrives: a sound you hear from another window, the taskbar icon flashing, and a notice.

items.label: Battleground helper
items.desc: A small bar at the top of the screen while you wait for a battleground: how long you have waited and the game's estimate, then how long the invitation has left. When you are in, a countdown to the start of the battle. /fgui bgscore shows the score.

items.label: Holidays on the checklist
items.desc: A holiday that is on in the game's calendar is added to your checklist as a daily job, and taken off when it ends. /fgui events lists what is on now and in the next two weeks.

items.label: Guild and friend notices
items.desc: The guild message of the day as a notice when you log in or it changes, and a notice when a friend or guild mate comes online.

items.label: Boss kill & achievement screenshots
items.desc: Takes a screenshot when a boss dies and when you earn an achievement.

items.label: Loot roll frames
items.desc: Our Need / Greed / Pass frames when loot is rolled for.

items.label: Loot rolls: light the button to press
items.desc: On the loot roll frames, the button to press lights up and the reason shows beside the item: Need for an item on your wishlist or an upgrade for you (with by how many item levels), Pass for gear you can't use, Greed for the rest. Nothing is ever rolled for you.

items.label: Tell me when an update is out
items.desc: People in your guild or group who also run Fantasy Glass UI tell each other which version they have. If someone has a newer one, you are told once. Only the version number is sent, and nothing during combat.

items.label: AFK screen
items.desc: While you are away: the interface fades, the camera drifts, and a panel shows session statistics.

items.label: Screenshot on level up
items.desc: Takes a screenshot each time you gain a level.

items.label: Chat improvements
items.desc: Short channel names, class-colored names, timestamps and wheel scrolling in chat.

items.label: Chat look
items.desc: The chat window's background and lettering in our style.

items.label: Chat links & copy button
items.desc: Clickable web links, a Copy button on each chat tab, and chat history after a reload.

items.label: Chat: class-colored names
items.desc: Player names in chat take their class color. This switches on the game's own setting for it.

items.label: Chat: highlight my name
items.desc: When someone else says your character's name in say, yell, party, raid, guild or a channel, the name is picked out in a bright color. Whispers are left alone.

items.label: Chat: sound when my name is said
items.desc: Also plays the whisper sound when your name is said (at most once every three seconds). Needs "Chat: highlight my name".

items.label: Chat: keep lines across a reload
items.desc: The last 40 lines of each chat tab are saved when you log out or reload, and shown again, dimmed, if you are back within half an hour. The combat log is not kept. Needs "Chat links & copy button".

items.label: Chat: typing bar above the chat
items.desc: Puts the bar you type in above the chat box instead of under it. Above, it lies over the chat tabs while you type, so they can't be clicked until you finish. Needs "Chat improvements".

items.label: Chat bubbles
items.desc: Speech bubbles over characters' heads in our style.

items.label: Names on chat bubbles
items.desc: Shows the speaker's name above each chat bubble.

items.label: Chat: keyword alerts
items.desc: Words you choose are picked out in green in any channel, with a sound. Choose them with /fgui keyword and the word.

items.label: Chat: hide repeated lines
items.desc: The same line from the same person within ten seconds is shown once (say, yell and channels).

items.label: Chat: Alt-click a name to invite
items.desc: Alt-click a name in chat to invite that player. The right-click menu of a player gains Copy name and Guild invite, where the game allows.

items.label: Whisper window
items.desc: Whispers open in a window with a tab for each conversation and a line to answer in. It never pops up during a fight. /fgui whispers opens it.

items.label: Short commands (/rl, /rc, /tt)
items.desc: /rl reloads the interface, /rc starts a ready check, /tt whispers your target. Each is left alone if another add-on already has it.

items.label: Friends list in class colors
items.desc: Friends who are online are listed in their class color, with level and zone.

items.label: Notes on players
items.desc: Your own note on any player, shown in their tooltip and when they join your group. /fgui note and the text, with the player targeted.

items.label: Ready-check report
items.desc: When a ready check starts, lists anyone missing food, a flask or elixir, or a class buff someone in the group can give. Only outside a fight. /fgui ready shows it any time.

items.label: Remember recent group mates
items.desc: Remembers the last forty people you grouped with. /fgui recent lists them: click to whisper, right-click to invite.

items.label: Group join and leave notices
items.desc: A line in chat and a sound when someone joins or leaves your group, and when a party is full.

items.label: Roll tracker
items.desc: Gathers everyone's /roll. /fgui rolls shows them highest first and names the winner; only 1-100 and a player's first roll count.

items.label: One-window bags
items.desc: All your bags in one window with categories, search and sorting.

items.label: Upgrade arrows on loot and quest rewards
items.desc: A green arrow on gear with a higher item level than what you wear in that slot: on loot rolls, quest rewards and the game's own bags (the one-window bags always have it). Item tooltips say by how much. /fgui equipbest puts on every upgrade that is already bound to you.

items.label: Looted an upgrade: a button to put it on
items.desc: Loot an upgrade and a small notice shows it, with by how many item levels it beats what you wear and a button to put it on. For a ring or a trinket there is a button for each of the two you wear. In a fight the click waits for the fight to end; an item not yet bound to you is put on only once the game has asked you. Move the notice with /fgui move.

items.label: One-window bank
items.desc: The bank in one window, in the same style.

items.label: Remember bags & bank
items.desc: Remembers each character's bags and bank so you can look at them from any character (/storage).

items.label: Bags: BoE tag on unbound gear
items.desc: Marks gear in your bags that binds when equipped and is not bound to you yet, so it can still be sold or traded.

items.label: Bags: coin on junk
items.desc: Puts a small coin on every item in the bag window that "Sell junk" would sell: gray items and anything on your always-sell list, less your never-sell list.

items.label: Bags: use items in combat
items.desc: Off until you choose it. Lets you use potions and other items from the bag window during a fight. While you are in combat the bag window's arrangement is frozen (icons and counts still update) and it re-sorts when the fight ends. If your client can't support it, it switches itself back off and says so in /fgui check.

items.label: Bags: mark gear set items
items.desc: An item that belongs to a gear set saved in the equipment manager says "Set" in the bag window, and is never sold with your junk.

items.label: Loot log
items.desc: Keeps a list of everything you loot this session. /fgui loot shows it with what a vendor would pay for it all.

items.label: Profession cooldowns
items.desc: Remembers each character's once-a-day crafts (transmutes and the like) whenever a profession window is open, and says when one is ready again. /fgui profcd lists them for all your characters.

items.label: Profession leveling helper (Skill-ups)
items.desc: A Skill-ups button on the profession window: the recipes you know that still give skill points, best first. What you can make now comes first, then what needs the fewest materials (counting your other characters), orange before yellow before green.

items.label: Bags: my own rules
items.desc: The sections you make yourself with the bag rules below (or /fgui bagrules). They come first: the first rule an item meets decides its section.

items.label: Bags: Upgrades section
items.desc: Gear better than what you wear (the green arrow) gets its own section at the top of the bags.

items.label: Bags: Gear sets section
items.desc: Items in a gear set from the equipment manager are kept together in a Gear sets section.

items.label: Bags: Bind on equip section
items.desc: Gear that binds when equipped and is not yet bound to you, so it can still be sold or traded, in a section of its own.

items.label: Bags: materials by kind
items.desc: Trade goods split by kind: Cloth, Leather, Ore and stone, Herbs, Cooking ingredients, Elemental, Enchanting materials and Gems, each its own section.

items.label: Bags: potions, food and scrolls apart
items.desc: Consumables split into Potions and elixirs, Food and drink, Scrolls and Bandages.

items.label: Bags: Recipes section
items.desc: Recipes, patterns, plans and formulas in a section of their own.

items.label: Auto-sell gray items
items.desc: Sells gray items whenever you open a vendor.

items.label: Auto-repair
items.desc: Repairs your gear whenever you open a vendor that can.

items.label: Repair from guild funds first
items.desc: Auto-repair pays from your guild allowance when it covers the whole bill, and from your own gold otherwise. Needs "Auto-repair". Presets never change this.

items.label: Vendors: one-line summary
items.desc: When you close a vendor, one line in chat says what the visit came to: what you sold, bought and repaired, and the total. It takes the place of the junk seller's and auto-repair's own lines.

items.label: Vendors: Alt-click buys a stack
items.desc: Hold Alt and click an item at a vendor to buy a full stack of it, or as many as you can afford.

items.label: Vendors: mark what I already know
items.desc: At a vendor, anything on sale that you have already learned (a recipe, a pattern, a mount, a pet) is washed in red, so you don't buy it twice.

items.label: Trainers: Learn all button
items.desc: Adds a "Learn all" button to the trainer window. It buys every skill you can learn and afford, one after another.

items.label: Mailbox helpers
items.desc: Buttons at the mailbox to collect all gold or open everything.

items.label: Mail: list my other characters
items.desc: While you are writing a letter, lists your other characters beside the mail window. Click one to address the letter to it.

items.label: Vendors: restock list
items.desc: Things you always want with you: /fgui restock, the item and a number. Whenever a vendor sells one, the difference is bought.

items.label: Auction prices in tooltips
items.desc: Remembers the lowest price you last saw or scanned for each item at the auction house and shows it in the item's tooltip.

items.label: Scan prices button
items.desc: A Scan prices button on the auction house reads every auction at once (the auction house allows it about every 15 minutes) for the prices in tooltips and the Sell now, Hold and Vendor it hints. It also reads full scans made by other add-ons.

items.label: Sell now, Hold and Vendor it hints
items.desc: In item tooltips: Sell now when an item is well above its usual price, Hold when it is cheap today, Vendor it when a vendor pays about as much or nobody lists it. Every Vendor it hint is for common and uncommon items only. On the bag window, a small square says the same: green for Sell now, amber for Hold, grey for Vendor it. From the prices you have seen and scanned.

items.label: Prices from Auctionator and TSM
items.desc: When this add-on has no price for an item, the tooltip shows Auctionator's price, or else TSM's, with its name beside it, if that add-on is loaded. Such a price is never kept, and gives only Vendor it (when a vendor pays about as much), never Sell now or Hold. Shown in tooltips while Auction prices in tooltips is on.

items.label: Auction house helper
items.desc: At the auction house: a "Lowest -1c" button on the sell page, and "Worth selling" (or /fgui ah), what in your bags sells for more there than at a vendor. Uses the prices you have seen, so search once first.

items.label: Gold ideas at the auction house
items.desc: Beside the auction house, a panel of ways to make gold with what this character has. It loads the gold folder the first time you open the auction house; off, the auction house loads and shows nothing of it.

items.label: Trade log
items.desc: After a trade, a line in chat says what changed hands and with whom. /fgui trades lists the last fifty.

items.label: Mail: Send by my rules button
items.desc: A "Send by my rules" button above the mail window whenever there is something to send. It sends everything below that is switched on, twelve items to a letter.

items.label: Mail: my own rules
items.desc: Your own mail rules, below (or /fgui mailrules), are sent too.

items.label: Mail: send cloth
items.desc: Cloth is sent to the character typed beside "Cloth" below. Soulbound items are never sent.

items.label: Mail: send leather
items.desc: Leather is sent to the character typed beside "Leather" below.

items.label: Mail: send ore and stone
items.desc: Ore, stone and bars are sent to the character typed beside "Ore and stone" below.

items.label: Mail: send herbs
items.desc: Herbs are sent to the character typed beside "Herbs" below.

items.label: Mail: send cooking ingredients
items.desc: Meat, fish and other cooking ingredients are sent to the character typed beside "Cooking ingredients" below.

items.label: Mail: send elemental materials
items.desc: Elemental materials are sent to the character typed beside "Elemental" below.

items.label: Mail: send enchanting materials
items.desc: Dusts, essences and shards are sent to the character typed beside "Enchanting materials" below.

items.label: Mail: send gems
items.desc: Gems are sent to the character typed beside "Gems" below.

items.label: Mail: send potions and food
items.desc: Potions, elixirs, food and other consumables that are not soulbound are sent to the character typed beside "Potions and food" below.

items.label: Accept invites from friends & guild
items.desc: Accepts a group invitation by itself when it comes from a friend, a Battle.net friend or a guildmate. Anyone else's invitation is left for you to answer. Presets never change this.

items.label: Faster auto-loot
items.desc: When auto-loot is in effect (your game setting, or the auto-loot key held), takes everything from a corpse at once instead of one item at a time. Presets never change this.

items.label: Type DELETE for me
items.desc: When you destroy a good item the game asks you to type DELETE. This types it for you; you still press the button to confirm. Presets never change this.

items.label: Skip cutscenes I have seen
items.desc: Skips a cutscene you have already seen once. The first time, it plays as normal. Hold Ctrl as one starts to watch it again. Presets never change this.

items.label: Pick the only choice when talking
items.desc: When a character offers exactly one thing to say and no quests, it is chosen for you. Never inside a dungeon or raid; hold Shift to choose for yourself. Presets never change this.

items.label: Follow the reputation I earn
items.desc: When you gain reputation with a faction, the reputation bar switches to that faction. Presets never change this.

items.label: Stand up when an action needs it
items.desc: When something fails because you are sitting down, you are stood up, so the next press works. Presets never change this.

items.label: Dismount when an action needs it
items.desc: When something fails because you are mounted, you are taken off your mount, so the next press works. Never in the air and never on a flight path. Presets never change this.

items.label: Accept resurrections
items.desc: Accepts a resurrection for you. One cast by someone who is in a fight is left on screen for you to time yourself. Hold Shift as the offer arrives to answer it yourself. Presets never change this.

items.label: Accept summons
items.desc: Accepts a summon for you after five seconds, saying in chat who it is from and where it leads. Decline it in that time to stay; hold Shift as it arrives to answer it yourself. Presets never change this.

items.label: Greed on green items
items.desc: When a group roll starts for a green (uncommon) item, Greed is rolled for you. Left for you to decide: anything blue or better, anything that binds when picked up, and gear with a higher item level than what you are wearing. Presets never change this.

items.label: Gear sets follow my talent set
items.desc: Each talent set remembers the gear set you last put on while it was active (with the gear set buttons or the game's equipment manager). Switch talent sets and that gear set goes on by itself. Nothing to set up. Presets never change this.

items.label: Invite by whisper
items.desc: A friend or guildmate who whispers you the word inv is invited to your group, whenever you are able to invite. /fgui invword changes the word. Presets never change this.

items.label: Whisper invites: from anyone
items.desc: With "Invite by whisper" on: anyone who whispers the word is invited, not only friends and guildmates. Presets never change this.

items.label: Decline duels
items.desc: Turns down duel requests for you and says in chat who asked. Hold Shift as one arrives to answer it yourself. Presets never change this.

items.label: Confirm bind-on-pickup loot alone
items.desc: When you loot alone, the question "Looting this item will bind it to you" is answered for you. In a group it stays a question. Hold Shift as you loot to be asked all the same. Presets never change this.

items.label: Accept role checks
items.desc: When the group finder asks everyone to confirm their role, yours is confirmed as you last set it. Hold Shift as the check arrives to answer it yourself. Presets never change this.

items.label: Maximum camera distance
items.desc: Lets the camera zoom out as far as the game allows. A game setting: switching this off puts back what it was. Presets never change this.

items.label: Mute the error voice
items.desc: Silences your character's spoken complaints ("Not enough mana", "I can't do that yet"). The red text stays. A game setting: switching this off puts back what it was. Presets never change this.

items.label: Sound when tabbed out
items.desc: Keeps the game's sound playing while you are in another window, so you hear a whisper or a ready check. A game setting: switching this off puts back what it was. Presets never change this.

items.label: Best-quality screenshots
items.desc: Saves screenshots at the game's best quality. A game setting: switching this off puts back what it was. Presets never change this.

items.label: Auto loot
items.desc: Takes everything from a corpse or chest as soon as you open it; hold Shift to look first. A game setting: switching this off puts back what it was. Presets never change this.

items.label: Loot window at the mouse
items.desc: Opens the loot window where your mouse pointer is, instead of at the side of the screen. A game setting: switching this off puts back what it was. Presets never change this.

items.label: Auto self-cast
items.desc: A helpful spell cast with no friendly target lands on you instead of asking for a target. A game setting: switching this off puts back what it was. Presets never change this.

items.label: Nameplates from further away
items.desc: Shows nameplates out to 41 yards, the furthest the game allows, so you see enemies before they reach you. It never shortens a longer distance. A game setting: switching this off puts back what it was. Presets never change this.

items.label: Stacking nameplates
items.desc: Nameplates stack above each other instead of overlapping, so in a crowd each one can be read and clicked. A game setting: switching this off puts back what it was. Presets never change this.

items.label: Camera stays where you turn it
items.desc: The camera no longer swings back behind your character on its own while you move. A game setting: switching this off puts back what it was. Presets never change this.

items.label: Clear weather
items.desc: Turns rain, snow and sandstorms down to nothing, for a clearer view and a steadier frame rate. A game setting: switching this off puts back what it was. Presets never change this.

items.label: Lower frame rate when tabbed out
items.desc: Holds the game to 30 frames a second while it is in the background, so your computer runs cooler and quieter. A game setting: switching this off puts back what it was. Presets never change this.

items.label: No tutorial pop-ups
items.desc: Stops the game's beginner tips and tutorial arrows. A game setting: switching this off puts back what it was. Presets never change this.

items.label: Profanity filter off
items.desc: Shows chat as people typed it, without the game's word filter. A game setting: switching this off puts back what it was. Presets never change this.

items.label: Mute the music
items.desc: Turns off the game's music; effects, voices and ambience stay. A game setting: switching this off puts back what it was. Presets never change this.

items.label: Mute ambient sounds
items.desc: Turns off background sounds such as wind, birds and crowds. A game setting: switching this off puts back what it was. Presets never change this.

items.label: No gray screen when dead
items.desc: The world keeps its colors while you are dead or a ghost. A game setting: switching this off puts back what it was. Presets never change this.

items.label: Less screen glow
items.desc: Turns off the soft full-screen glow, for sharper edges and a little more speed. A game setting: switching this off puts back what it was. Presets never change this.

items.label: Lower graphics in raids
items.desc: Shadows, liquid detail, particle density and a few other costly settings are turned down while you are inside a raid and put back when you leave.

items.label: Fishing mode
items.desc: While a fishing pole is equipped: sound effects at full, music and background noise down, auto-loot on. Everything goes back when the pole comes off.

items.label: Combat log in raids
items.desc: Starts the game's combat log file when you enter a raid and stops it when you leave (only if this started it).

items.label: Combat log: dungeons too
items.desc: The same in five-player dungeons.

items.label: Hide the talking head
items.desc: Hides the box with a face that speaks during some quests. The voice still plays.

items.label: Move the talking head
items.desc: Lets you place that box in move mode.

items.label: Use quest guides
items.desc: The step panel, and the arrow that points to your step. Off, nothing of the guide shows.

items.label: A sound when a step is done
items.desc: A short sound each time a step ticks off.

items.label: Include elites my class has soloed
items.desc: Elite quests that one of your characters of this class has done alone count as Solo quests.

items.label: Plan class quests
items.desc: Your class quests go on the route at the right level, and the panel says when one is ready.

items.label: Learn new flight points on the way
items.desc: A short way round to a flight master you do not know yet, when the route passes close.

items.label: Visit your trainer on the way
items.desc: A stop at your class trainer every two levels, for your new spells.

items.label: Save hand-ins to level in town
items.desc: A hand-in that would take you up a level waits until the route reaches your trainer's town.

items.label: Sell and repair stops
items.desc: A stop at a vendor when your bags are nearly full or your gear is worn.

items.label: Buy supplies at the vendor stop
items.desc: At that stop, ammunition, food and drink are bought too.

items.label: Profession training stops
items.desc: A stop at a profession's trainer when your skill has reached what you can learn now.

items.label: Mount reminder
items.desc: From level 40: the riding trainer, your mount, and how much gold is still to find.

items.label: Mail stops
items.desc: A stop at a mailbox when mail is waiting and one is close.

items.label: Explore on the way
items.desc: Places you have not discovered yet, when they are close to the route.

items.label: Gather on the way
items.desc: Herbs and ore you have gathered before, close to the route, and a note to skin what you kill.

items.label: Show the best quest reward
items.desc: At a hand-in, the reward that suits you best is marked and named in chat. You choose it yourself.

items.label: Count upgrades in rewards
items.desc: A quest whose reward is better than what you wear counts for more.

items.label: Quest log advice
items.desc: When your quest log is nearly full, the panel says which quests are worth abandoning.

items.label: Suggest an inn when you stop
items.desc: After a long stretch of play, the panel points to an inn close by, to log out in for rested experience.

items.label: Count rested experience
items.desc: Kills are worth double while you are rested, and the route counts them so.

items.label: Suggest what to do when quests run dry
items.desc: When no quest is worth the trip, a dungeon or a place to grind is suggested instead.

items.label: Learn from my deaths
items.desc: A place where you died twice is left alone until you are two levels higher.

items.label: Show why each step is there
items.desc: Each step on the panel says what it is worth: the experience, or the time it saves.

items.label: Remind me to take a break at a stopping place
items.desc: After a long stretch of play, the panel says so when you reach a good place to stop.

items.label: Keep my route
items.desc: Levelling up, hand-ins and loading screens leave the route as it is. Only Plan my route and Plan again make a new one.

items.label: The route on the map
items.desc: The route's stops, numbered, and the line between them on the world map.

items.label: Quest areas on the map
items.desc: A mark on each area with quests the planner found, brighter where the experience comes faster.

items.label: Use TomTom's arrow when TomTom is loaded
items.desc: The step you are on goes to TomTom's arrow instead of this add-on's.

items.label: Race your best
items.desc: The panel says how far ahead or behind you are of your fastest character's time at this level.

items.label: Where you left off, at login
items.desc: When you log in, a line says where you were on the route and what comes next.

items.label: Read the route aloud
items.desc: Each new step is read aloud as you reach it.

items.label: Find a group button
items.desc: A group quest on the panel gets a button that writes a line asking for a group. It only fills your chat box: you send it.

items.label: Let friends ask to plan with you
items.desc: A friend with Fantasy Glass UI can ask to plan one route for you both. You are always asked first. Only your friends, your guild and your group can ask, once in 5 minutes each.

commands.desc: open the options (or use the minimap button)
every command in a window you can search; click one to put it in the chat box
arrange your panels; right-click one for its own settings
put back the last panel move, nudge, resize or reset
run the guided setup again
the settings at Tools: every window, and things to do once
every tool window in one small panel (also "Tools" on the Menu button)
Frames and bars: each action bar's size, opacity, when it shows, rows and spacing
keybind mode: hover an action button and press a key
every action bar with its keys (or hold the key you bind for it)
whole screen layouts to choose from, each with a picture
the short tour of the interface
point at any panel to see which feature made it
ask the guide where something is, in a few words
fill the screen with samples, to see everything at once
hide the interface for a few seconds (for screenshots)
quiet mode: no chat, names or info bar, for screenshots and streaming (again to undo)
choose the add-on's language
what changed in this version
your quest guides: follow one, write or paste one, or record one as you play (record <name>, stop, next, back, off)
plan a route of quests for your level and follow it; with a number, a route that fits the time you can play
the planner window: the route you follow, Keep my route, and every setting for what the planner plans
change, move or take out the steps of the guide you are following
plan one route with a friend who has the add-on (/fgui guide duo off to stop)
your route as a plan code to copy, to read on the website's plan page
the guide panel's menu, to use with the keyboard
ways to make gold: ideas for this character, each with Go, which plans the trip (or Ctrl-click the minimap button)
who in your group is missing food, a flask or a class buff
are you ready for the raid: food, flask, weapon, repairs, reagents, bag space, talents and gear
your target's boss note, to read or write (/fgui bossnote send: to the group; list: all of them)
what hit you before you last died
your group's roles, classes and who covers each buff
who in your group is not here
everyone's /roll, highest first ("clear" starts a new round)
a pull countdown for everyone in the group (/fgui break 5 is a break, in minutes)
the order your group takes turns interrupting (empty: everyone, A to Z)
group practice: made-up group mates, to see group cooldowns, the interrupt rotation and buff coverage alone
screenshot mode: every frame with sample data and nothing in the way; again to end
the loot browser: what each boss dropped, with the upgrades for you first
your wishlist: the items you starred in the loot browser, and where each drops
a farming session: time, and gold and item value an hour; again to see it, stop to end it, zones for your best spots
show or hide the threat meter
lifetime stats: time played, quests, kills, deaths, gold, loot, bosses and runs, for this character and all of them
everyone in your group with their item level, the lowest first, and the group's average
your dungeon and raid runs: times, bosses, wipes, deaths and loot, with the best time for each place
put on a gear set by name (part of the name will do); on its own, the list of your sets
order the raid frames by group, role or name
reset your instances and tell the group
tuck the damage meter drawer away, or bring it out
clear the damage meter
the battleground's score
where the execute line sits on the target's health bar
an icon while that buff is missing (again to stop)
leave that buff out of your buff row (again to show it)
never show that buff or debuff on the unit frames, raid frames or nameplates (again to show it)
your last week on every character: gold, time played, levels, raids and dungeons, best loot ("this": this week so far)
what is waiting for you: crafts ready, mail on your other characters, lockouts reset, rested experience, jobs left
your characters, with level and gold, and the total
make this character your main: new characters copy its setup
this session's statistics and time played, with your last session
your gold day by day, and where this session's went
your daily and weekly jobs for each character; /fgui checklist add daily <job>
which raids and dungeons each character is saved to
once-a-day crafts on all your characters, and when each is ready
with a profession window open: the recipes that still give skill points, best first, with what each needs
what all your characters can craft; search their recipes
reputations and currencies on all your characters; click one to pin it
change talent set
keep your talents as a build; /fgui talents lists them, click one to import it
send a saved talent build to another player of your class
put on every upgrade in your bags (higher item level, already bound to you)
sort your bags in the order of your bag sections (again to stop)
a bag section by rule (ilvl, boe, set, quality, type, name)
always sell that item with your junk (shift-click the item in)
never sell it;  /fgui sell list shows both lists
always keep that many: bought at any vendor who sells it
what in your bags is worth more at the auction house than at a vendor
put every crafting material in the bank (bank open)
add the selected recipe to the crafting queue; /fgui queue list shows it
what the selected recipe still needs, counting bank and alts
everything looted this session and its vendor value
the trades on record
mail rules; "Send by my rules" at the mailbox sends them
goals: /fgui goal rep <name>, gold 10000, level 60, mount <name>, or an item and a number
a goal of your own on the goals panel (click it to count); /fgui goal ach <achievement> too
a note on the player you have targeted ("list" shows them all)
the people you grouped with lately: whisper or invite
the whisper window
make a Loot tab and a Whispers tab
pick that word out in chat, with a sound (again to stop)
the word a whisper must be for an invite (see "Invite by whisper")
send your layout (or profile, or theme) to another player who has the add-on
